reasoning: I checked each part of the claim against the code and none of it holds up as a false alarm. wrapProgressCallback (download-stats.ts:57-67) skips progress only when collector.cacheHit === true. Otherwise it records max(fileSetInfo.overallDownloaded ?? shardInfo.overallDownloaded ?? downloaded). Nothing records the bytes already on disk at the start, so nothing is subtracted. computeStats (102-108) then reports that value as totalBytesDownloaded and divides it by elapsed time to get downloadSpeedBps. I confirmed each source the reviewer named. (1) http.ts:229-230 sets downloadedBytes = startOffset, the size of the partial file already on disk. When the server answers 206, the counter is not reset (it resets only for a non-206 reply, lines 302-306). The data handler then emits downloaded: downloadedBytes, which includes the prefix (393-397). The 416 branch (283-289) is worse: no cache hook is called, so cacheHit stays undefined, and it emits downloaded: startOffset. That reports the whole file as downloaded in roughly zero time. (2) In the HTTP sharded path, cached shards get downloadedBytes = expectedSize (780-784), markCacheMiss is called when any shard is missing (793), and overallDownloaded adds up every shard (1010). (3) In Hyperdrive, markCacheMiss runs at hyperdrive.ts:585, then already-valid files add their size to overallDownloaded and report it in progress (618-638). registry.ts:216 and registry-companion-set.ts:122 do the same thing, so the problem is wider than the reviewer said. These paths are reachable through the public loadModel/download flow whenever a download resumes or some shards are already cached. No caller or wrapper corrects for it. The comment at line 58 says cache-hit bytes should not count as network transfer, which shows this behaviour is not intended. No test sets an expected value for totalBytesDownloaded. The impact is limited to profiling gauges (types.ts:86-87, operation-metrics.ts:60-61) and does not affect downloads or model loading, so low severity is right.
